Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router). You are making real code edits (not just investigating) to 11 marketing page files. Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first for repo conventions (esp. "Working on this codebase" and doc-update requirement).

BACKGROUND: Nxeon's VPS catalog (`db.plan`, Prisma) used to have a cheapest tier called "Nano" priced at $6.49/mo. It has since been renamed/repriced — the current live cheapest VPS tier is "Starter" with `priceCents=1598` ($15.98 regular) and `introPriceCents=888` ($8.88 intro/first-term rate, `introTermMonths=null` meaning the WHOLE first term is discounted, not just one month). The other VPS tiers are Standard (intro $12.99, regular $23.38), Pro (intro $20.99, regular $37.78), Max (intro $32.99, regular $59.38) — verify these are still current yourself by running a temp script (see credential-hygiene rule below) before you rely on them, in case they've changed since this was written.

Eleven marketing page files still contain the STALE hardcoded literal "$6.49" and/or "Nano" typed directly into prose (title/metadata/sub/why-cards/steps/specNote/FAQ) — completely disconnected from the live database, so it no longer matches reality and won't reflect the next price change either:

1. `app/(marketing)/cheap-vps-hosting/page.tsx`
2. `app/(marketing)/affordable-vps-hosting/page.tsx`
3. `app/(marketing)/best-value-vps/page.tsx`
4. `app/(marketing)/wordpress-vps-hosting/page.tsx`
5. `app/(marketing)/docker-hosting/page.tsx`
6. `app/(marketing)/vpn-server-hosting/page.tsx`
7. `app/(marketing)/nodejs-hosting/page.tsx`
8. `app/(marketing)/n8n-hosting/page.tsx`
9. `app/(marketing)/discord-bot-hosting/page.tsx`
10. `app/(marketing)/nextcloud-hosting/page.tsx`
11. `app/(marketing)/free-vps/page.tsx`

All 11 share an IDENTICAL structure: a module-level `const content: UseCaseContent = { ... }` object with hardcoded "$6.49"/"Nano" strings woven through it, a static `export const metadata: Metadata = { ... }` also containing "$6.49", and a default async page component that does `const plans = await db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" } }); return <UseCaseLanding content={content} plans={plans} />;`. `UseCaseLanding` (in `components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx`) renders `content` as prose sections and separately renders `<PricingGrid plans={plans} />` — that PricingGrid part is being fixed by someone else in parallel to show live intro pricing correctly, so DO NOT touch `components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx` or `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx` — your job is ONLY the hardcoded prose/metadata in these 11 page files themselves.

A shared helper already exists for you at `/opt/nxeon/lib/marketing/cheapest-vps.ts` — read it first. It exports `cheapestVpsPricing(plans: {name:string; priceCents:number}[])` which returns `{ planName, fromLabel, renewsLabel } | null`: `fromLabel` is the correct live lowest price string (e.g. "$8.88"), `renewsLabel` is the renewal price string (e.g. "$15.98") or `null` when there's no intro discount, and `planName` is the real current plan name (e.g. "Starter", NOT "Nano").

YOUR TASK, for EACH of the 11 files:

1. Add `import { cheapestVpsPricing } from "@/lib/marketing/cheapest-vps";` (adjust relative path if `@/` alias doesn't resolve in this file — check an existing import in the same file to confirm the alias works; it does throughout this codebase).

2. Convert the static `export const metadata: Metadata = {...}` into an async `export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {...}` that fetches `db.plan` itself (same query as the page component), computes `const pricing = cheapestVpsPricing(plans);`, and replaces every literal "$6.49" inside the title/description/OG fields with `${pricing?.fromLabel ?? "$6.49"}` (keep a safe fallback string in case the catalog is ever empty — the OLD hardcoded value is an acceptable last-resort fallback here, not a live claim). Follow the exact async `generateMetadata` pattern already used in `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` in this repo for structure/style consistency — look at that file for the idiom.

3. Convert the module-level `const content: UseCaseContent = {...}` into a function `function buildContent(pricing: ReturnType<typeof cheapestVpsPricing>): UseCaseContent { return {...}; }` (or equivalent — keep it a plain function, not exported). Inside, replace:
   - every literal "$6.49" with `${pricing?.fromLabel ?? "$6.49"}`
   - every literal "Nano" (the plan name) with `${pricing?.planName ?? "Nano"}`
   - Additionally, in the FIRST place a headline price appears in flowing prose (typically the `sub` field, and/or the `specNote` field, and/or one FAQ answer that states "what does it cost") — wherever `pricing?.renewsLabel` is non-null, work in a short, honest renewal disclosure using this codebase's own established phrasing style for this exact concept. For reference, existing precedents in this codebase (do not copy verbatim, but match the register/tone): PricingExplorer.tsx's plan-card caption reads "Intro price for your first {term/month}, then $X/mo — renews at the regular price"; the FAQ-style phrasing already in cheap-vps-hosting's own content object is "New plans get an introductory discount off the first term, then renew at the regular monthly rate." A good pattern is something like: `` `${pricing.fromLabel}/mo for your first term${pricing.renewsLabel ? `, then renews at ${pricing.renewsLabel}/mo` : ""}` ``. Do NOT invent a "first month" framing — the correct term is "first term" (it may cover more than one month; that's a deliberate, previously-fixed nuance in this codebase, see `introTermMonths` in `lib/intro-pricing.ts`). Don't cram a renewal disclosure into every single one of the ~5 "$6.49" mentions per file (that would read as repetitive/broken) — one clear disclosure near the primary headline mention (the `sub` field is usually the best spot, since it is the large hero subheading right under the H1) is enough per page; the rest of the mentions can just use the corrected `fromLabel` number plainly.

4. Update the default exported async page component to compute `const pricing = cheapestVpsPricing(plans);` right after fetching `plans`, and call `buildContent(pricing)` instead of referencing the old static `content` constant, e.g.:
   ```
   export default async function XyzPage() {
     const plans = await db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" } });
     const pricing = cheapestVpsPricing(plans);
     return <UseCaseLanding content={buildContent(pricing)} plans={plans} />;
   }
   ```

5. Leave every OTHER hardcoded number in these files (e.g. mentions of "Standard (4 GB)" or "$12.99"/"$20.99" for the Standard/Pro/Max tiers, or generic feature copy) untouched UNLESS it's also a stale/wrong price for that tier — spot-check any other literal "$XX.XX" you encounter in these 11 files against the live DB values you queried in step 0, and fix only genuine mismatches the same way (interpolate from a live value; you may extend `cheapestVpsPricing`-style logic inline or just compute the specific tier's `planIntroMonthlyCents` value directly via `import { planIntroMonthlyCents } from "@/lib/intro-pricing"` if a page references a specific non-cheapest tier by price). Do not go on a broader hunt beyond these 11 files — that's handled separately.

6. `free-vps/page.tsx` has an unusually large number of "$6.49"/"Nano" mentions (its whole premise is "here's what it costs after any free credit ends") — apply the same substitution pattern throughout; it's mechanically the same fix, just more occurrences in that one file.

CREDENTIAL HYGIENE: if you need to check current DB values yourself, write a script under `/opt/nxeon/scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run via `npx tsx` from `/opt/nxeon`. Never construct or print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` connection string. Delete the temp script when done.

VERIFICATION: after editing all 11 files, run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` and fix any type errors your changes introduced before finishing. Do NOT run `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon` itself (see CLAUDE.md's build-isolation note — building in the live prod tree can clobber prod's `.next`); typecheck only. Do NOT commit, push, or deploy anything — someone else in this session owns the final commit/deploy step once all the parallel work (including yours) lands. Do NOT touch `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — the coordinating session will add the single combined changelog entry covering this whole batch of pricing fixes.

Report back concisely: confirm all 11 files were edited, list any additional stale-price mismatches you found and fixed beyond the "$6.49"/"Nano" pattern (with specifics), and confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` passes clean.

7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
96	- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
97	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
98	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.
99	
100	## Safety rules
101	
102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
103	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
104	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
105	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
106	- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
107	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
108	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

2	 * VPS INTRO PRICING — a LOW first-term price that RENEWS at the regular price
3	 * (classic hosting promo: "$3.99/mo first term, renews at $6.49/mo").
4	 *
5	 * This is deliberately modelled as a FIRST-TERM-ONLY discount so it rides the
6	 * plumbing the platform already has, rather than adding a second renewal price:
7	 *
8	 *   - The ORDER (lib/order.ts) charges the intro-reduced first term and stamps the
9	 *     implied first-term rate on `Server.termPromoPercent` (the very column every
10	 *     later proration/refund already prices against — see lib/proration.ts).
11	 *   - RENEWAL (lib/renewal-charge.ts — the SINGLE renewal formula) reads
12	 *     `plan.priceCents` and knows NOTHING about `introPriceCents`, so a renewal is
13	 *     billed at the regular price by construction. No renewal code changes.
14	 *
15	 * Pure & deterministic (no `db`, no I/O), so it can be imported by the order core,
16	 * the marketing pricing cards and unit tests alike. The two READERS below cast to
17	 * reach `introPriceCents` / `introTermMonths` because the symlinked prod Prisma
18	 * client's types predate these columns until it is regenerated at deploy — the
19	 * same stale-client gap `frozenProductAnnualPct` (lib/product-billing.ts) and the
20	 * `Server` writes in lib/order.ts already work around. Identical at runtime once
21	 * the client is regenerated.
22	 */
23	import { termDiscountPct } from "./billing-terms";
24	
25	/** A row that MAY carry the intro columns (present at runtime, absent from stale types). */
26	type PlanIntroFields = { introPriceCents?: number | null; introTermMonths?: number | null };
27	
28	/**
29	 * The plan's intro MONTHLY price in cents, or null when it is unset, malformed, or
30	 * NOT genuinely below the regular price. Requiring `intro < regular` means a bad /
31	 * equal / higher value can never quietly RAISE the first-term charge — it just
32	 * disables the intro and the plan bills its regular price.
33	 *
34	 * `plan` is typed loose on the intro column because the symlinked prod Prisma client's
35	 * types predate it (regenerated at deploy); the value is present at runtime.
36	 */
37	export function planIntroMonthlyCents(plan: { priceCents: number }): number | null {
38	  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields).introPriceCents;
39	  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 0) return null;
40	  const cents = Math.round(v);
41	  if (cents >= plan.priceCents) return null;
42	  return cents;
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * How many of the first term's months are billed at the intro rate. NULL / invalid
47	 * => the WHOLE first term (returned as null so callers apply it across every month).
48	 * Clamped to >= 1 so a stray 0 can never zero the intro window. `plan` is `unknown`
49	 * for the same stale-client reason as above.
50	 */
51	export function planIntroTermMonths(plan: unknown): number | null {
52	  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields | null | undefined)?.introTermMonths;
53	  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 1) return null;
54	  return Math.round(v);
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Cents knocked off the FIRST term because of the intro rate — 0 when there is no
59	 * intro. Expressed as a REDUCTION of the regular term total (not a second price)
60	 * so the regular term price stays the single source of truth and the renewal math
61	 * is untouched:
62	 *
63	 *   discount = (regularMonthly − introMonthly) × introMonths × (1 − termDiscount)
64	 *
65	 * `introMonths` is `min(introTermMonths ?? months, months)`, so a 1-month term is
66	 * fully intro-priced, and a "$3.99 first month" intro on a 12-month first order
67	 * discounts exactly one month and bills the other eleven at the regular rate.
68	 * The term discount is applied so the intro months are discounted consistently
69	 * with the rest of the term the customer chose.
70	 */
71	export function introFirstTermDiscountCents(
72	  regularMonthlyCents: number,
73	  introMonthlyCents: number | null,
74	  termMonths: number,
75	  introTermMonths: number | null,
76	  annualDiscountPct?: number,
77	): number {
78	  if (introMonthlyCents == null || introMonthlyCents >= regularMonthlyCents) return 0;
79	  const months = Math.max(1, Math.round(termMonths));
80	  const introMonths = introTermMonths != null ? Math.min(introTermMonths, months) : months;
81	  if (introMonths <= 0) return 0;
82	  const pct = termDiscountPct(months, annualDiscountPct);
83	  return Math.max(0, Math.round((regularMonthlyCents - introMonthlyCents) * introMonths * (1 - pct / 100)));
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * The percent OFF the regular term total that the intro first term represents,
88	 * as a whole number 0..100 — the value stamped on `Server.termPromoPercent` so
89	 * proration and refunds price against the rate the term was actually sold at.
90	 * Integer because it round-trips through Stripe metadata as an integer promo
91	 * percent (lib/order.ts parseOrderPrice), exactly like the seasonal promos.
92	 */
93	export function introSoldPercent(regularTermCents: number, introDiscountCents: number): number {
94	  if (regularTermCents <= 0 || introDiscountCents <= 0) return 0;
95	  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round((introDiscountCents / regularTermCents) * 100)));
96	}
